SK2113 The service resolution is null-forgiven instead of required

GetService<T>()! suppresses the warning that says the service may not be registered; GetRequiredService<T>() throws where the mistake is.

CategoryCorrectness
Default severitysuggestion
ScopeSemantic
Needs a compilationyes
Runs under --load=looseno
Cached per fileyes
Fixyes, safe
Language version floor—
Since2.0

Why

GetService<T>() returns null for a service nobody registered, and the ! is the author asserting that somebody did. When the assertion is wrong the program does not fail at the resolution — it fails at the first use, with a NullReferenceException that names neither the service type nor the container. GetRequiredService<T>() is the same call with the assertion moved into the framework: it throws an InvalidOperationException naming the service type, at the line that asked for it. The ! is not redundant here, which is why SK2111 declines it; it is the wrong answer to a real warning.

Example

Instead of:

var clock = provider.GetService<IClock>()!;

Write:

var clock = provider.GetRequiredService<IClock>();

When it does not fire

⚠ The generic extension only. provider.GetService<T>() and GetKeyedService<T>() on Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection.ServiceProviderServiceExtensions are reported, in either call form, because the fix is a rename inside a class the call site has already resolved — so the using that made the call compile makes the fix compile. provider.GetService(typeof(T))!, the IServiceProvider interface method, is declined: its GetRequiredService counterpart lives in an extension class the file may not have imported, and a fix that does not compile is worse than no fix. ⚠ The nullable context does not silence this rule. It reads the ! token and the callee's symbol, never a flow state, so it reports the same code under #nullable disable — where the mistake is identical and the compiler is silent. ⚠ Only where the `!` is written. GetService<T>() whose result is null-checked, coalesced or assigned to a nullable local is the API used correctly and is never reported. ⚠ A user-defined GetService<T> on some other type is not this method and is resolved by containing type rather than by name.
